sheet-1.description: The lower half of the title sheet of the June 1928 Raritan atlas, drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the upper half carries the key map, the street and specials index, a location map of New Jersey and notes on water facilities and the fire department, and is not part of this map. The mapped area is the western edge of the borough between Frelinghuysen Avenue at the top and the Central Railroad of New Jersey along the bottom. Raritan Avenue, Quick Avenue, Gaston Avenue and 1st Avenue run north and south and are crossed by Farrand Street and Tillman Street, with the ends of 6th Street and 5th Street at the right edge where the map continues on sheet 7. The blocks are lettered A to I and are only lightly built up: scattered frame dwellings and small outbuildings, mostly along Quick, Gaston and 1st Avenues, with large empty lots between them, a laundry on Gaston Avenue and a fire alarm box at 1st Avenue and 5th Street. West of Raritan Avenue the Bridgewater Township line runs down the sheet, and beyond it, in block 120, stand the works of the Raritan Radiator Company, manufacturers of steam boilers and castings: a foundry with an earth floor, a pattern making shop, a machine shop and shipping building of brick and steel, and a sand bin beside a siding. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches are shown in Farrand and Tillman Streets. A scale bar and a north arrow are drawn in the open ground at the left.
notes: Frelinghuysen Avenue west of Victoria Street is now part of US 202; its junctions were not used.
Gaston Avenue here is North Gaston Avenue today.
6th Street west of 2nd Avenue is now Farrand Street; 5th Street is Fifth Street.
Raritan Radiator Co. foundry and machine shop lie in Bridgewater Township, west of the borough line.

Top half: index, key map (900 ft to an inch), water and fire notes (masked out). Bottom half: map at 100 ft to an inch of the west end: Frelinghuysen Av, Farrand, Tillman, Raritan Av, Quick Av, Gaston Av, 1st Av, 5th and 6th St, Bridgewater Township line, Raritan Radiator Co foundry, C.R.R. of N.J. One part.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the western part of the old village south of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, at 50 feet to an inch. Gaston Avenue and 1st Avenue run down the sheet and are crossed by 3rd Street, 2nd Street and Burns Street; Church Street runs south from 2nd Street to 1st Street, which cuts diagonally across the bottom right corner, where North Wall Street begins; 2nd Avenue forms the right edge. The upper left quarter is open ground occupied by the railroad's turntable with its radiating tracks. Above 3rd Street on the east side of 1st Avenue is the vacant plant of the Raritan Radiator Company and the Frank Gallager coal yard with coal sheds and wagon sheds along the tracks. The rest of the sheet is dense residential building: rows of frame dwellings, two-family houses and stores on narrow lots along 1st Avenue, Gaston Avenue and 3rd and 2nd Streets, with a brick terrace of dwellings on the east side of 1st Avenue south of 2nd Street, a hall on 2nd Street and a few auto houses and sheds in the backs of lots. The large block east of Church Street holds Public School No. 1 and Public School No. 2, both of brick with steam heat and electric light. Water pipes of 3 to 6 inches are marked in most streets, with hydrants and a fire alarm box at 1st Avenue and 2nd Street. A scale of feet is drawn at the bottom right.
notes: 1st Avenue is First Avenue and 2nd Street is Second Street in OpenStreetMap.
Frank Gallager coal yard and the vacant Raritan Radiator Co. plant lie on the north side of 3rd Street along the railroad.

Pilot. Gaston Av, 1st Av, 3rd St, 2nd St, Church St, Burns, 1st St, N. Wall St, 2nd Av; Raritan Radiator Co vacant plant, Frank Gallager coal yard, C.R.R. of N.J. turntable, Public Schools No. 1 and 2. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 is at 50 feet to an inch and covers the centre of the old village between the Central Railroad of New Jersey at the top and 1st Street at the bottom, from 2nd Avenue on the left to North Thompson Street on the right. Anderson Street runs down the middle of the sheet and 2nd Street crosses it; 3rd Street, La Grange Street and Colfax Street come in from the sides as short stubs. The railroad's main tracks run diagonally across the top, with the Central Railroad of New Jersey station, a freight office and waiting room, and a platform east of Anderson Street, and a siding curving south into the yard of the Consumers Supply and Coal Company, with lumber sheds, piles of lumber, a building material shed and a mill work shop. West of Anderson Street the blocks hold frame dwellings and stores, the Star of Italy Hall and St. Anna's Roman Catholic Church. South of 2nd Street the blocks are commercial and denser: brick stores and dwellings, a club, a moving picture theatre, a bakery, an auto repairing garage, a creamery, a second bakery and the Central Hotel on North Thompson Street, with auto sheds behind. Water pipes, hydrants and a fire alarm box near the station are marked, and a scale of feet is drawn at the bottom.
notes: North Thompson Street is Thompson Street in OpenStreetMap; La Grange Street keeps its name.
1st Street ends at Anderson Street from the west; its junction was hand-picked because the detector placed it on a lot line about 40 ft north.
The railroad crossing at Anderson Street was rejected by the fit (track layout changed).
2nd Av, Anderson, N. Thompson, 3rd St, 2nd St, 1st St, La Grange St, Colfax St; C.R.R. of N.J. station, Consumers Supply and Coal Co, St. Anna R.C. Church. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 is at 50 feet to an inch and covers the southwest part of the village down to the Raritan Canal and the Raritan River. West Somerset Street crosses the middle of the sheet; Gaston Avenue and 1st Avenue run up to Burns Street at the top left, 1st Street runs along the top right to North Wall Street, and below West Somerset Street, Lyman Street, Nevius Street and South Wall Street run down to Canal Street, which follows the north bank of the canal. Small Brook runs down the left edge. North of West Somerset Street the blocks hold dwellings, tenements, a blacksmith and welding shop, the Agostino Grasso pants factory, the J. Lapinsky body builder's shop, a bakery and an auto repairing shop, and at the right St. Bernard's Parochial School and hall. South of the street are rows of frame dwellings with a club and a filling station. The canal, marked for water power only, and the wide river fill the lower half; an iron bridge carries Nevius Street over both. Between them stand the J. B. Duke filter plant and the J. B. Duke electric lighting station with its pump house, and at the bottom right the Sommerville Water Company pumping station with a filter house, standpipe and tail race. Water pipes, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked, and a scale of feet is drawn at the bottom left.
notes: 1st Avenue north of West Somerset Street and Lyman south of it are First Avenue and Lyman Street today; they meet West Somerset Street at one junction.
The Sommerville Water Co. pumping station is spelled Sommerville on the sheet.
Gaston Av, 1st Av, Lyman, Nevius, N. and S. Wall, W. Somerset, 1st St, Burns, Canal; Raritan Canal and River, J.B. Duke filter plant and electric lighting station. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 is at 50 feet to an inch and covers the business centre of Raritan along West and East Somerset Street, from North and South Wall Street on the left to North and South Thompson Street on the right, between 1st Street at the top and Canal Street and the Raritan Canal at the bottom. Anderson Street runs up from Somerset Street, and Loomis Street and Doughty Street run down to Canal Street. North of Somerset Street are the post office, St. Bernard's Roman Catholic Church and rectory, stores, a bank, the fire department hose house of Relief Hose No. 2 with a lockup, and the 3rd Reformed Dutch Church of Raritan with its Sunday school. South of it are the Centennial Hotel, the Harcar Hotel, the Methodist Episcopal Church and chapel, the 1st Slovak Evangelical Lutheran Church, a second bank, drug stores and an undertaker, with dwellings behind. Below Canal Street the canal, marked for water power only, curves across the sheet; south of it are the works of D. R. Kenyon and Son, makers of textile machinery, with a foundry, machine shops and pattern storage, the J. B. Duke private pumping station, closed, and the Raritan Woolen Mills. A steel bridge crosses the canal below Loomis Street. Water pipes up to 36 inches, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked; a north arrow and a scale of feet are drawn in the open ground.
notes: West and East Somerset Street are West Somerset Street and East Somerset Street; North and South Thompson are Thompson Street in OpenStreetMap.
The Raritan Woolen Mills are marked Mutual Risk, admittance and plans refused.
N. and S. Wall, Anderson, Loomis, Doughty, N. and S. Thompson, W. and E. Somerset, 1st St, Canal; Raritan Canal, D.R. Kenyon and Son, J.B. Duke pumping station, Raritan Woolen Mills. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 is at 50 feet to an inch and covers the eastern part of the village south of the railroad, from North and South Thompson Street on the left to Wyckoff Avenue and the Lagrange Street boundary on the right. Lagrange runs along the top, Colfax crosses the left half, and East Somerset Street crosses the sheet below the middle; Lincoln Street runs diagonally up the centre beside a freight switch of the woolen mills, and Codington Street, Reimer Street and Frederick Street run north and south through the right half, with Elizabeth Street and Glacier Avenue at the bottom. The left half holds the Gaffner skirt and dress factory, the Slavonian Hotel, a large concrete block garage for twenty-five cars, a hall and stores near Thompson Street, and south of East Somerset Street St. Joseph's Slovak Church, its rectory and St. Joseph's Parochial School. The right half is a newer residential district of frame dwellings on narrow lots. A base ball ground fills the block between Lincoln Street and Frederick Street south of East Somerset Street, and along Elizabeth Street at the bottom runs the long brick building of the Somerset Manufacturing Company's woolen mill, marked mutual risk. A coal yard lies along the switch. Water pipes, hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked; a north arrow and a scale of feet are drawn at the bottom.
notes: Codington is Coddington Street and Glacier Avenue is Glaser Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Lagrange is La Grange Street.
Lincoln south of East Somerset Street continues as the curved road along the base ball ground, now John Street.
The Somerset Mfg Co's woolen mill along Elizabeth Street is cut by the bottom edge.

N. and S. Thompson, Lincoln, Codington, Reimer, Frederick, Wyckoff, Lagrange, Colfax, E. Somerset, Elizabeth, Glacier Av; Gaffner skirt factory, St. Joseph's church and school, Somerset Mfg Co woolen mill. One part.

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of sheet 7, below the heavy dividing line, is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the north side of the village between Frelinghuysen Avenue at the top and the Central Railroad of New Jersey at the bottom, from 1st Avenue on the left to Victoria Street on the right. 2nd Avenue and Anderson Street run diagonally down the left half and North Thompson Street down the middle; 6th Street, 5th Street, Farrand Street and Tillman Street come in at the left, and Bell Avenue, Sherman Avenue and Railroad Avenue cross the right half. Below the tracks, North Thompson Street and Lagrange appear at the bottom right with a long brick row of dwellings. The area is a recent subdivision of narrow numbered lots, most of them still empty: frame dwellings stand scattered along 1st Avenue, Anderson Street, Bell Avenue and Sherman Avenue, with a terrace of brick dwellings on 5th Street, a shirt factory near the railroad between 2nd Avenue and Anderson Street, and a few auto houses. The blocks are numbered 25 to 43. A strip of lots north of Frelinghuysen Avenue is shown up to the dividing line. Water pipes, hydrants and a fire alarm box at 1st Avenue and Tillman Street are marked, with a north arrow on Frelinghuysen Avenue and a scale bar at the bottom.
notes: 6th Street is now part of Farrand Street; 5th Street is Fifth Street; Frelinghuysen Avenue here is now US 202.
2nd Avenue junctions on this part disagree with the fit by 5 to 6 m and were left out; US 202 junctions disagreed by 7 to 8 m (the road has been widened).

100 ft to an inch. Main part (below the heavy line): Frelinghuysen Av to the C.R.R. of N.J., 1st Av to Victoria, with Lagrange at bottom right. Inset top right (part 2): Summit, West End Av, North Av, Cornell Blvd north of Frelinghuysen near the Somerville line. Inset top left (part 3): J.S. Frelinghuysen estate, own north arrow.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: J.S. Frelinghuysen estate and Mrs E.L. Birdsall property (top left, own north arrow) (no street junction or identifiable modern street; location relative to the main map not drawn; needs hand-picked parcel corners after identifying the estate on the ground (step 6b)).

sheet-7-2.description: The inset at the top right of sheet 7, separated from the main map by heavy lines, is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and shows the northeastern corner of the borough north of Frelinghuysen Avenue, against the Somerville line. West End Avenue runs diagonally from the upper left to the corner of Frelinghuysen Avenue and Cornell Boulevard, along the Bridgewater Township line, which is lettered along it. North Avenue runs from Summit at the top down to West End Avenue, and Cornell Boulevard, a 100-foot street, runs down the right side with the Borough of Somerville line beside it and Altamount Avenue leaving it to the east. The area is a subdivision of long narrow lots in blocks 123 to 127 and 35, with frame dwellings scattered along West End Avenue and North Avenue and a few at the top near Cornell Boulevard; most lots are empty. A strip south of Frelinghuysen Avenue, with the corner of the block at Cornell Boulevard, is drawn down to the dividing line and repeats the top of sheet 8. Water pipes of 6 inches run in Frelinghuysen Avenue, West End Avenue and Cornell Boulevard. The inset carries no north arrow of its own; it is drawn square to the main map.
notes: North Avenue is probably Northwood Avenue today; Altamount Avenue is Altamont Place; Summit is West Summit Street.
Placed from three block corners carried from sheet 8 and two detected junctions on West End Avenue, with the scale and rotation of sheet 7; low confidence.

Inset top right (part 2): Summit, West End Av, North Av, Cornell Blvd north of Frelinghuysen near the Somerville line. Inset top left (part 3): J.S. Frelinghuysen estate, own north arrow.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and covers the northeastern part of Raritan from Frelinghuysen Avenue at the top to East Somerset Street and Glacier Avenue at the bottom, between Victoria Street on the left and Cornell Boulevard and the Borough of Somerville line on the right. Southwick runs down the left half; Bell Avenue and Sherman Avenue cross the upper part, and Railroad Avenue, marked not open, runs along the north side of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which crosses the middle of the sheet with a switch tower. West End Avenue and the Bridgewater Township line cut the top right corner. The upper half is a subdivision of narrow numbered lots in blocks 34 to 45, almost all empty, with a few frame dwellings and a filling station at the corner of Cornell Boulevard. Below the tracks Lagrange runs across the sheet, Codington Street, Reimer and Elmer, also lettered Elmore, run down to East Somerset Street, and George and Wyckoff lead to Glacier Avenue. These blocks are built up with rows of frame dwellings, with a clothing factory beside the tracks near the Somerville line and sheds near the bottom right. Water pipes up to 36 inches run in East Somerset Street. A north arrow is drawn at the left and a scale bar at the bottom right.
notes: Codington Street is Coddington Street and Glacier Avenue is Glaser Avenue in OpenStreetMap; George Street is not in the modern data (the corner is now taken by US 206).
Elmer is also lettered (Elmore).
Bell Avenue beyond the Somerville line meets Cornell Boulevard at a second modern node, which was excluded.

100 ft to an inch. Frelinghuysen Av to E. Somerset and Glacier Av, Victoria to the Somerville borough line: Bell, Sherman, Railroad Av, Southwick, Cornell Blvd, Lagrange, Reimer, Elmer, George, Wyckoff, Codington St; C.R.R. of N.J. One part.
